sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余味》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: Back in the mists of time when we were mere podcasting novices, when we recorded our very first episode, we hit on the subject of greatness.
sentences.zh: 回想我们刚开始做播客时，还是个纯粹的新手，录制第一期节目时，我们谈到了“伟大”这个主题。

sentences.en: And today's podcast is about a man we talked about a lot in that first episode without ever really getting into his story.
sentences.zh: 而今天的播客要讲一个人，我们在第一期节目里频繁提到他，却从未真正深入讲述过他的故事。

sentences.en: And it is probably the greatest story in all history.
sentences.zh: 这大概是整个人类历史上最伟大的故事了。

sentences.en: It is, of course, Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 他当然就是亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: There's probably no greater character, no better story, no more glamour and excitement and romance than in the life of Alexander, is there?
sentences.zh: 亚历山大的一生，恐怕没有比这更伟大的人物、更好的故事、更具魅力、更令人兴奋和浪漫的了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a great story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的故事。

sentences.en: I thought it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I was surprised that when I put the note up on Twitter saying we were going to do Alexander the Great, the response was absolutely overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 让我惊讶的是，当我在推特上发帖说我们要讲亚历山大大帝时，反响简直太热烈了。

sentences.en: I don't think we've ever had as many replies or questions, have we?
sentences.zh: 我想我们从来没收到过这么多回复或提问，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think we had more questions even for Hitler than we did for Alexander.
sentences.zh: 我觉得即使是讲希特勒时，收到的问题也没有讲亚历山大时多。

sentences.en: And Sam, a heroic kind of backroom boy who he was basically ploughing through hundreds of questions in order to try and whittle them down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 还有山姆，这位幕后的英雄，他基本上是在处理成百上千个问题，试图把它们精简一下。

sentences.en: Well, I was reassured and I'll tell you why.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时很放心，我告诉你为什么。

sentences.en: It was because I went to this fantastic literary festival held at Patrick Lee Firmer's house on the shore of the
sentences.zh: 因为我参加了一个很棒的文学节，地点就在帕特里克·利·弗莫尔（Patrick Leigh Fermor）位于

sentences.en: Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 伯罗奔尼撒半岛的家中。

sentences.en: And there was a kind of parlour game type thing in the evening where we all had to make an argument for who was the greatest Greek.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上有个类似客厅游戏的东西，我们每个人都要为“谁是最伟大的希腊人”进行辩论。

sentences.en: And obviously I chose Alexander the Great because he's great.
sentences.zh: 显然我选择了亚历山大大帝，因为他很伟大。

sentences.en: And I thought, I'm just going to, of course, I'm going to watch this.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我当然要看看这个。

sentences.en: And Bethany Hughes chose Helen of Troy and we came joint bottom.
sentences.zh: 贝瑟妮·休斯（Bettany Hughes）选了特洛伊的海伦，结果我们并列垫底。

sentences.en: Oh no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Who won?
sentences.zh: 谁赢了？

sentences.en: Aristophanes because he would have opposed Brexit.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯托芬，因为他会反对英国脱欧。

sentences.en: That's a terrible, that's such an indictment to that whole occasion.
sentences.zh: 那太糟糕了，那简直是对整个活动的控诉。

sentences.en: So that may reflect the fact that I made a terrible case for him and I think I did rather.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能反映出我为他做的辩护很糟糕，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think it also reflects a kind of tension in attitudes towards Alexander now that we actually discussed in our very firSt. He is obviously, I mean, he's a great figure.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这也反映了现在人们对亚历山大的态度中存在一种张力，我们在第一期节目里其实讨论过。他显然是个伟大的人物。

sentences.en: He's the essence of greatness.
sentences.zh: 他是伟大的本质。

sentences.en: He's the first person to be called great.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个被称为“大帝”的人。

sentences.en: That's the whole point of him.
sentences.zh: 这正是他的意义所在。

sentences.en: But there's a slight ambivalence now towards him that perhaps wasn't there earlier.
sentences.zh: 但现在人们对他有一种微妙的矛盾心理，这在过去可能并不存在。

sentences.en: So there was this whole kind of, the heyday of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 在大英帝国鼎盛时期，人们有这种想法。

sentences.en: There was this idea that he was selflessly conquering the world for the good of the subject people, which obviously went down rather well.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种观点认为，他为了被征服人民的利益而无私地征服世界，这显然很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And now that kind of attitude is
sentences.zh: 而现在，那种态度

sentences.en: viewed with a certain degree of a sconce.
sentences.zh: 被视为带有某种轻蔑。

sentences.en: It's a tremendous adventure story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的冒险故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think you've got a question from Stephen Clark.
sentences.zh: 我想你有一个来自斯蒂芬·克拉克的提问。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Sorry, I'm just queuing you up.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我正在帮你排队。

sentences.en: I don't know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, so I do.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，我想起来了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a question from Stephen
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个来自斯蒂芬·

sentences.en: Clark, a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 克拉克的问题，他是节目的朋友。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Great man.
sentences.zh: 伟人。

sentences.en: Great man in his own right.
sentences.zh: 他本人也是个伟人。

sentences.en: A friend of Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克的朋友。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a shameful question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个令人羞愧的问题。

sentences.en: It's the top question that Sam chose of all the questions.
sentences.zh: 这是山姆从所有问题中选出的头号问题。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: You put it at the top of the sheet.
sentences.zh: 你把它放在了表格的最上面。

sentences.en: Oh God, I'm losing the will to live.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我都要失去活下去的动力了。

sentences.en: Why did Dominic choose Alexander the Great as one of his Adventures in Time series?
sentences.zh: 为什么多米尼克选择亚历山大大帝作为他《时间冒险》系列的主题之一？

sentences.en: So Dominic, Adventures in Time.
sentences.zh: 所以多米尼克，《时间冒险》。

sentences.en: This is your series of children's books.
sentences.zh: 这是你的儿童读物系列。

sentences.en: You did an earlier one on Henry VIII on the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 你之前写过关于亨利八世和二战的。

sentences.en: You've got one on the First World War, which is why we're going to be doing Remembrance Sunday as our next episode.
sentences.zh: 你还有一本关于一战的，这就是为什么我们下一期节目要讲阵亡将士纪念日。

sentences.en: It's a complete coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这纯属巧合。

sentences.en: It's a massive coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的巧合。

sentences.en: And you've chose Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 而你选择了亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: What story did you have to miss out or severely edit to ensure your book about Alexander is appropriate for children?
sentences.zh: 为了确保你的亚历山大书适合儿童阅读，你不得不删掉或大幅修改哪些故事？

sentences.en: Funnily enough, I don't think I really did have to miss any stories out.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我觉得我真的不需要删掉任何故事。

sentences.en: Did you miss out Bagoas?
sentences.zh: 你删掉巴戈阿斯（Bagoas）了吗？

sentences.en: Bagoas actually has been massively inflated.
sentences.zh: 巴戈阿斯其实被过度夸大了。

sentences.en: So Bagoas is the Persian eunuch that he supposedly has an affair with.
sentences.zh: 巴戈阿斯是那个据传与他有染的波斯太监。

sentences.en: One of the top eunuchs who appeared in our...
sentences.zh: 出现在我们节目中的顶级太监之一……

sentences.en: He was one of our top eunuchs.
sentences.zh: 他是我们最顶级的太监之一。

sentences.en: Bagoas' appearance and the sources are slight at beSt.
sentences.zh: 巴戈阿斯的出现以及史料记载充其量是微不足道的。

sentences.en: So did you leave him out?
sentences.zh: 所以你把他删了吗？

sentences.en: Fleeting.
sentences.zh: 转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: So I think I pretty much...
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我基本上……

sentences.en: No, there's one fleeting mention of him that when I'm talking about Alexander adopting Persian customs, that he's got a great friend called Bagoas.
sentences.zh: 不，我提到过他一次，就在我讲亚历山大采纳波斯习俗时，提到他有个好朋友叫巴戈阿斯。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: A great pal.
sentences.zh: 好哥们。

sentences.en: But no, I think, why did I choose it?
sentences.zh: 但没有，我想，我为什么选这个？

sentences.en: Well, why are we doing it on this podcast and why are we going to give it two episodes?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们为什么要在这个播客里讲他，为什么要用两期节目来讲他？

sentences.en: I mean, the answer is because it is probably the single most exciting story in all history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，答案是因为这可能是整个人类历史上最令人兴奋的故事。

sentences.en: I think the only one that would really compare would be the arrival of...
sentences.zh: 我想唯一能与之相比的可能就是……

sentences.en: It's the Persian invasion of Greece.
sentences.zh: 波斯入侵希腊。

sentences.en: I would not say that.
sentences.zh: 我不会这么说。

sentences.en: Not even Watergate.
sentences.zh: 甚至连水门事件都比不上。

sentences.en: Or indeed, the Jeremy Thorpe scandal.
sentences.zh: 或者杰里米·索普丑闻。

sentences.en: I would say it's probably the arrival of the conquistadors in the New World.
sentences.zh: 我会说这大概相当于征服者来到新大陆。

sentences.en: For the sheer kind of...
sentences.zh: 因为那种纯粹的……

sentences.en: Drama.
sentences.zh: 戏剧性。

sentences.en: ...almost science fiction level drama.
sentences.zh: ……几乎是科幻小说级别的戏剧性。

sentences.en: I mean, the idea that Alexander, you know, he fights his first major battle when he's 18, when he's 20, he's king.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，亚历山大在18岁时打赢了第一场大战，20岁时就成了国王。

sentences.en: He leads his men for a decade on this
sentences.zh: 他带领部下进行了长达十年的

sentences.en: unbelievably strange and exacting journey where they go to places that they've...
sentences.zh: 难以置信的奇异而严苛的旅程，他们去了那些他们……

sentences.en: They could barely imagine.
sentences.zh: 几乎无法想象的地方。

sentences.en: They're climbing these mountains.
sentences.zh: 他们翻越这些山脉。

sentences.en: They see the pyramids.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了金字塔。

sentences.en: They travel for...
sentences.zh: 他们旅行了……

sentences.en: I think historians have worked out they keep going for about 22,000 miles and they just keep going.
sentences.zh: 我想历史学家计算过，他们总共走了大约22000英里，而且一直在走。

sentences.en: And at the end, they think they're going to...
sentences.zh: 最后，他们以为他们要……

sentences.en: He thinks he's going to get to the end of the earth.
sentences.zh: 他以为他要走到世界的尽头。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an incredible story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: And in the course of it, he conquers...
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，他征服了……

sentences.en: He defeats the world's most biggest and richest empire.
sentences.zh: 他击败了世界上最大、最富有的帝国。

sentences.en: He becomes king of kings.
sentences.zh: 他成为了万王之王。

sentences.en: He enters unchallenged, the greatest city on earth.
sentences.zh: 他毫无阻碍地进入了地球上最伟大的城市。

sentences.en: He thinks he's a god.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己是神。

sentences.en: I mean, what's not to like?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有什么理由不喜欢呢？

sentences.en: It's just a tremendous, tremendous quest narrative.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个了不起的探索叙事。

sentences.en: And I think it's one of those stories that you read about it as a child and it gets you into history for life.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是那种你小时候读过，就会让你终身热爱历史的故事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of story I think that teenagers in their 20s put away because they're a bit embarrassed by it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种青少年在20多岁时会束之高阁的故事，因为他们觉得有点尴尬。

sentences.en: They don't want to do a seminar on it.
sentences.zh: 他们不想就此进行研讨。

sentences.en: And then they come back to it later on and they're like, damn, it's a good story.
sentences.zh: 然后他们后来又回过头来看，觉得：该死，这真是个好故事。

sentences.en: So I think lots of...
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多……

sentences.en: You know, we've talked about this before.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们之前谈过这个。

sentences.en: Lots of people, myself included, kind of get into history and perhaps particularly ancient history through the mythology, Greek mythology.
sentences.zh: 很多人，包括我自己，都是通过神话，希腊神话，开始接触历史，尤其是古代史。

sentences.en: You read the Trojan War and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你读了特洛伊战争之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then you want a sequel.
sentences.zh: 然后你想要续集。

sentences.en: And in a way, Alexander is the sequel.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，亚历山大就是续集。

sentences.en: And he's a sequel, I think, for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是续集有两个原因。

sentences.en: Partly because he consciously models himself on Achilles.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他在有意识地以阿喀琉斯为榜样。

sentences.en: So he claims to be descended from Achilles and from Heracles, two great heroes.
sentences.zh: 所以他声称自己是阿喀琉斯和赫拉克勒斯的后裔，这两位伟大的英雄。

sentences.en: So ultimately, he's the descendant of Zeus.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，他是宙斯的后裔。

sentences.en: So he's wired into that world of mythology.
sentences.zh: 所以他与那个神话世界紧密相连。

sentences.en: He models himself on Achilles.
sentences.zh: 他以阿喀琉斯为榜样。

sentences.en: He takes Iliad with him on his great adventures and so on.
sentences.zh: 他带着《伊利亚特》进行伟大的冒险，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But I think also
sentences.zh: 但我认为还有一点

sentences.en: it's because actually the story of Alexander the Great is
sentences.zh: 是因为亚历山大大帝的故事实际上

sentences.en: it is a kind of myth because actually the sources for it are a lot more patchy, precarious and late than one might want to think.
sentences.zh: 它本身就是一种神话，因为实际上关于他的史料比人们想象的要零碎、不可靠且晚得多。

sentences.en: And we on our episode of Mohammed and really the story of Arab conquest is the only comparison to this.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于穆罕默德的那期节目里说过，阿拉伯征服的故事是唯一能与此相比的。

sentences.en: If you think, you know, Macedon is on the margins of great empires and it conquers these great empires rather in the way that the Arabs do in the 7th and 8th centuries.
sentences.zh: 如果你想，马其顿处于大帝国的边缘，它征服了这些大帝国，就像7、8世纪的阿拉伯人所做的那样。

sentences.en: And just as the sources for the Arab conquests are late, kind of centuries later, and therefore the
sentences.zh: 正如关于阿拉伯征服的史料很晚，是几个世纪后的产物，因此

sentences.en: kind of stories that you get with lots of arrows and maps and things and people confidently saying
sentences.zh: 你看到的那些带有许多箭头、地图和人们自信地说

sentences.en: that the Arabs did this and they did that, you know, you've got to slightly kind of raise an eyebrow at that.
sentences.zh: “阿拉伯人做了这个，做了那个”的故事，你得稍微挑挑眉毛（表示怀疑）。

sentences.en: Same is slightly true for Alexander because I think the earliest account narrative account of his life is 300 years after it.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大的情况也差不多，因为我认为关于他生平最早的叙事记载是在他死后300年才出现的。

sentences.en: Most of the accounts that we draw on are actually written in the heyday of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们所引用的绝大多数记载实际上都是在罗马帝国鼎盛时期写成的。

sentences.en: So in a sense are as much about the Romans as they are about Alexander himself.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，它们既是关于罗马人的，也是关于亚历山大本人的。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So and on top of that, there's a further complication which is that we have all and this is something again that we talked about in the Thermopylae episode, we have
sentences.zh: 而且最重要的是，还有一个进一步的复杂因素，那就是我们拥有——这也是我们在温泉关战役那期节目中谈到的——我们几乎

sentences.en: almost nothing, written sources from the Persian side.
sentences.zh: 没有任何来自波斯方面的书面史料。

sentences.en: And so a bit as in a kind of romance, a nightly romance, you get the knight going out and having the adventures and you don't hear about, you know, what the dragon thought of it.
sentences.zh: 所以就像在某种浪漫传奇、骑士传奇中，你看到骑士出去冒险，却听不到龙是怎么想的。

sentences.en: So likewise with this, he leads his armies, he attacks all these people, but it's like they are just kind of exotic names.
sentences.zh: 同样，他带领军队，攻击所有人，但这些人就像是异国情调的名字。

sentences.en: They're just the stormtroopers in Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 他们就像《星球大战》里的冲锋队。

sentences.en: Kind of, kind of.
sentences.zh: 差不多，差不多。

sentences.en: And I think, I think, I think that the great, you know, the kind of the great revolution,
sentences.zh: 我认为，我认为，我认为伟大的，你知道，那种伟大的革命，

sentences.en: the understanding of Alexander, and it was, it's been pointed out by various academics that
sentences.zh: 对亚历山大的理解，正如各种学者指出的那样，

sentences.en: the study of Alexander has, you know, in terms of sophistication has been, it's been a bit of a backwater for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 对亚历山大的研究，在复杂性方面，长期以来一直处于停滞状态。

sentences.en: And I think that that has really begun to change and it's chiefly begun to change because there are great scholars who have looked at the Persians and have tried to
sentences.zh: 我认为这种情况真的开始改变了，这主要是因为有伟大的学者研究了波斯人，并试图

sentences.en: place Alexander in the context of, of the world that he conquers.
sentences.zh: 将亚历山大置于他所征服的世界的背景中。

sentences.en: And perhaps the greatest of them is a French scholar called Pierre Brion.
sentences.zh: 其中最伟大的可能是一位名叫皮埃尔·布里昂（Pierre Briant）的法国学者。

sentences.en: He famously described Alexander as the last of the
sentences.zh: 他著名地将亚历山大描述为最后一位

sentences.en: Achaemenids and the Achaemenid is the Persian dynasty that Alexander overthrows.
sentences.zh: 阿契美尼德人，而阿契美尼德王朝正是亚历山大推翻的波斯王朝。

sentences.en: And I think that that actually does start to make sense of him as someone who is not, you know, a hero from myth and is not a
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实开始让他变得合理了，他不再是一个神话中的英雄，也不是一个……

sentences.en: kind of monster, which are the two poles that tend to kind of govern how he's understood, but someone who

sentences.zh: 但有些人说，正如亚历山大大帝故事的顶级儿童版所说，在孟菲斯的酒馆里，士兵们交换着流言蜚语。

sentences.en: And some people say that he says to them, have I sufficiently avenged the death of my father and killed Philip?
sentences.zh: 有些人说他对他们说，我是否充分为我父亲的死报了仇，杀死了腓力？

sentences.en: And have I got revenge over the Persians?
sentences.zh: 我是否向波斯人报了仇？

sentences.en: And they say, no, no, because your father is not Philip.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，不，因为你的父亲不是腓力。

sentences.en: Your father is Zeus.
sentences.zh: 你的父亲是宙斯。

sentences.en: And at that point, now the thing is, Tom, do you think he believes this?
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，问题是，汤姆，你认为他相信这一点吗？

sentences.en: Do you think he thinks he's the son of a god based on his subsequent conduct?
sentences.zh: 根据他随后的行为，你认为他认为自己是神的儿子吗？

sentences.en: Ah, I just don't think that.
sentences.zh: 啊，我真不这么认为。

sentences.en: It's going to give a very evasive answer.
sentences.zh: 这会给出一个非常闪烁其词的回答。

sentences.en: Well, OK, so there's an interesting answer to this, which is, have you seen this gold coin that was supposedly found down a well in Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，关于这个问题有一个有趣的答案，那就是，你见过那枚据说是从阿富汗的一口井里发现的金币吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: Is that one of them, I Karnum or one of those?
sentences.zh: 那是他们中的一个，还是卡努姆（Karnum）或者其他什么人？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, it's southern Afghanistan and there's a well.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，不，不，不，不，那是阿富汗南部，那里有一口井。

sentences.en: And they found a whole, supposedly a whole stash of a massive, massive hoard of coins.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一整批，据说是整整一大批，数量极其庞大的钱币。

sentences.en: And they kind of started turning up in the 1990s, I think on the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 我想是在塔利班时期，它们开始出现。

sentences.en: And these coins started turning up, filtering out.
sentences.zh: 这些钱币开始出现并流散出来。

sentences.en: And one of them is a gold coin, which has an elephant on one side and a picture of what's clearly Alexander on the other.
sentences.zh: 其中有一枚金币，一面刻着大象，另一面显然是亚历山大的肖像。

sentences.en: And he has a kind of elephant hood, a hood made of a scalped elephant.
sentences.zh: 他戴着一种象皮兜帽，是用剥下来的象皮做的。

sentences.en: And he has the horns of Amun.
sentences.zh: 他还长着阿蒙神的角。

sentences.en: And it seems likely because there are also a whole series of coins which were definitely minted in Alexander's lifetime,
sentences.zh: 这似乎很有可能，因为还有一系列钱币肯定是在亚历山大在世时铸造的，

sentences.en: showing elephants for reasons that will come to in due course when Alexander invades India.
sentences.zh: 上面展示了大象，原因我们稍后在亚历山大入侵印度时会讲到。

sentences.en: India.
sentences.zh: 印度。

sentences.en: And so the thesis is that this is a coin that dates, it's the only thing that dates from his lifetime.
sentences.zh: 所以结论是，这是一枚可以追溯到他生前的钱币，也是唯一一枚。

sentences.en: Because there are subsequent coins with him with ram's horns, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 因为后来还有他长着公羊角的钱币，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, which are minted by Ptolemy, as in, you know, Mr. Snake.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是托勒密铸造的，也就是那位“蛇先生”。

sentences.en: And Ptolemy has his own interest in branding Alexander as a god.
sentences.zh: 托勒密有他自己的动机，想把亚历山大包装成神。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然。

sentences.en: Because the Egyptians think of pharaohs as gods, right?
sentences.zh: 因为埃及人认为法老就是神，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, because Alexander, yes, but Alexander's body ends up in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为亚历山大，是的，但亚历山大的遗体最终留在了埃及。

sentences.en: So Ptolemy has a kind of massive interest in saying, I have the body of a god.
sentences.zh: 所以托勒密非常有动力去宣称：我拥有神的遗体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that, as you can tell from the talking snake stuff, quite a lot of these stories are not entirely reliable.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你从那些关于会说话的蛇的故事中所能看出的，这些故事中有很多并不完全可靠。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't tell me you're going to diss Ptolemy's reliability.
sentences.zh: 是啊，别告诉我你要质疑托勒密的可靠性。

sentences.en: So I think, to that extent, it's difficult to know.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在这一点上，很难下定论。

sentences.en: But if this coin is genuine, then that would suggest, and it's minted in Alexander's lifetime, then that would suggest that it is coming from Alexander himself.
sentences.zh: 但如果这枚钱币是真的，而且是在亚历山大在世时铸造的，那就说明它来自亚历山大本人。

sentences.en: That still doesn't mean that Alexander does necessarily believe it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着亚历山大本人一定相信这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it might be for propagandistic purposes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能纯粹是出于宣传目的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But I think the border, you know, in Greece, the border between the divine and the human is much more porous, much more amorphous than it is for us.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在希腊，神圣与凡人之间的界限比我们现在的要模糊得多，也更具流动性。

sentences.en: I think that's definitely true, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是真的，汤姆。

sentences.en: And I think as well, some historians say that Greece has been ever more tightly connected to Egyptian and Persian ideas of kingship in recent years,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，近年来一些历史学家也指出，希腊与埃及和波斯关于王权的观念联系得越来越紧密，

sentences.en: and the idea of a kind of sacral.
sentences.zh: 以及那种神圣的……

sentences.en: I'm using a Tom Holland word.
sentences.zh: 我正在用汤姆·霍兰（Tom Holland）的词汇。

sentences.en: Yeah, you are.
sentences.zh: 没错，你确实在用。

sentences.en: Of a kind of sacral kingship.
sentences.zh: 那种神圣王权的观念。

sentences.en: Welcome to my world.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到我的世界。

sentences.en: So when Philip was assassinated, going into the stadium, which we mentioned in the first half,
sentences.zh: 所以当腓力在进入体育场时被暗杀，正如我们在上半部分提到的那样，

sentences.en: he was about to join a procession of images of the gods.
sentences.zh: 他正准备加入一个神像的游行队伍。

sentences.en: There was going to be images of the Olympians and another image of Philip himself kind of as a god.
sentences.zh: 队伍里会有奥林匹斯众神的神像，还有一尊腓力本人作为神的神像。

sentences.en: So already that kind of idea that a king is very like a god, perhaps even godly or godlike, rather, I should say, is sort of in the ether.
sentences.zh: 所以，国王就像神一样，甚至可以说是神圣的，或者说具有神性的这种观念，已经在空气中弥漫了。

sentences.en: And so it kind of explains why Alexander might believe it in a sort of weird way.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上解释了为什么亚历山大可能会以一种奇怪的方式相信这一点。

sentences.en: And it's something that really kicks in in the decades after Alexander's death, where the Athenians, they greet this kind of warlord, Macedonian warlord, as a god.
sentences.zh: 这在亚历山大死后的几十年里真正爆发了，雅典人把这位军阀，这位马其顿军阀，当作神来迎接。

sentences.en: And they say, well, because you're on the earth and the other gods aren't, and we need to.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，因为你在地球上而其他神不在，我们需要……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's not a very good reason, I don't think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不是一个很好的理由。

sentences.en: That's quite a good reason.
sentences.zh: 这理由相当充分。

sentences.en: It's quite a good reason.
sentences.zh: 确实相当充分。

sentences.en: They greet him by carrying giant phalluses through the streets of Athens.
sentences.zh: 他们通过在雅典街头抬着巨大的男性生殖器雕像来迎接他。

sentences.en: I would find that a bit disconcerting, personally.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我会觉得这有点令人不安。

sentences.en: So, yes, those borders are porous.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那些界限是模糊的。

sentences.en: But I think, and I don't know whether this coin is, I think it's generally not thought to be authentic.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我不知道这枚钱币是否……我认为人们普遍认为它不是真品。

sentences.en: But there are very serious scholars who think it is.
sentences.zh: 但也有非常严肃的学者认为它是真的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I am not remotely qualified to judge a dream.
sentences.zh: 而我完全没有资格去评判一个梦。

sentences.en: See, I think Alexander's subsequent behaviour makes more sense if you think he thinks he's really touched by something.
sentences.zh: 你看，我认为如果你认为亚历山大觉得他真的被某种东西触碰过，那么他随后的行为就更说得通了。

sentences.en: Because this is the point I think.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为重点就在这里。

sentences.en: No, he's Achilles.
sentences.zh: 不，他是阿喀琉斯。

sentences.en: He's Achilles.
sentences.zh: 他是阿喀琉斯。

sentences.en: So, Achilles is a hero.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿喀琉斯是一位英雄。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've talked about this before.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们之前讨论过这个。

sentences.en: Hero.
sentences.zh: 英雄。

sentences.en: The idea of a hero is, you know, you are the son of a god or you have something of the divine about you.
sentences.zh: 英雄的概念是，你知道，你是神的儿子，或者你身上有某种神性的东西。

sentences.en: So, that is a status that is kind of universally recognised in the Greek world.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种在希腊世界被普遍认可的地位。

sentences.en: I'm sure Alexander thinks that he occupies that position, that he's a hero in that sense.
sentences.zh: 我相信亚历山大认为他占据了那个位置，他就是那种意义上的英雄。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But whether he thinks he's a god, I'm not possible to say.
sentences.zh: 但至于他是否认为自己是神，我无法断言。

sentences.en: So, we're at the end of this episode.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们这一集到此结束。

sentences.en: So, Alexander is there in Egypt with his mates.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚历山大和他的伙伴们在埃及。

sentences.en: Tom Holland's done a fantastic impersonation of the mate.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰对那位伙伴的模仿真是太精彩了。

sentences.en: Do you want to give us that one more time?
sentences.zh: 你要再给我们表演一次吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, top level.
sentences.zh: 好，顶级水平。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: There we go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And there they are with Prince Harry and the others.
sentences.zh: 他们和哈里王子以及其他人都在那里。

sentences.en: Gearing her up.
sentences.zh: 为她做准备。

sentences.en: They're all there in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 他们都在埃及。

sentences.en: Now, I think this is the point at which anybody else might have packed up and gone home.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这是其他人可能已经收拾行李回家的时候了。

sentences.en: But, of course, Alexander doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但当然，亚历山大没有。

sentences.en: He goes on.
sentences.zh: 他继续前进。

sentences.en: And what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: We will discover next time, won't we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我们下次再揭晓，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: If you have Pothos, you have Pothos.
sentences.zh: 如果你有渴望（Pothos），你就有渴望。

sentences.en: We'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余韵》（The Rest is History）。
